mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) level relative to the prior 3-month average signals monetary easing, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS is below the 3-month prior average.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in FEDFUNDS above 4.0% in the prior month signals monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and compressing equity valuations to produce negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Joint behavior of FEDFUNDS rising above 4.0% and CPIAUCSL falling below 3.0% signals disinflationary monetary tightening, reducing equity risk appetite and causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL < 3.0%.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.0%), a decline in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS declines.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1200.0 (thousands) signals weak consumer demand, reducing corporate revenue expectations and producing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where HOUST < 1200.0.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100.0 (index) signals manufacturing contraction, reducing corporate earnings growth and causing negative S&P 500 20-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where INDPRO < 100.0.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS over the prior 3 months relative to the 6-month average signals monetary easing, lowering discount rates and producing positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of months where FEDFUNDS declines by more than 0.5% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in residential sales (RSAFS) below 700,000 million dollars signals weak housing market demand, reducing construction activity and causing negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of months where RSAFS < 700000.
